log: DOES THE CELL HAVE SLACK -- and was the gate that said no asking the right question?
loop_medium's M3 counted a knockout as 'moving growth' if it changed mu by more than 1e-9.
That is a floating-point threshold, not a biological one. This audits my own gate first.
1,784 scored knockouts from loop 4's defined-medium model
DIAGNOSIS: 1,525 of 1,784 knockouts have a NEGATIVE cost, clustered at -7.25e-07.
A knockout cannot improve growth in this model, so that is arithmetic, not biology.
loop_medium calibrated the uptake cap by BISECTION and then used the bisection's last
iterate as mu_WT (0.029999790) instead of re-solving at the final bounds.
Every unaffected knockout then solved to a very slightly HIGHER mu, so 1 - mu_KO/mu_WT
came out at about -7e-07 -- and M3's `abs(diff) > 1e-9` test counted all 1,525 of
them as 'moving growth'. That is where 92% came from.
The fix for any future run is one line: re-solve mu_WT at the final bounds, or test
against a relative threshold rather than an absolute one.
P1 THE THRESHOLD SWEEP -- where does the answer change?
cost >     fraction moving growth
1e-09                     13.5%   <- loop_medium used this
1e-02                     11.7%   <- 1% of growth, a real effect
at a 1% cost threshold, 11.7% of deletions move growth   (gate < 50%)   P1 PASS
M3's failure WAS an artefact of the cutoff. The model does have slack; the gate was
counting numerical dust as biology. loop_medium's conclusion is restated accordingly.
P2 SHAPE -- against DepMap's own dependency fractions (1,775 genes with both)
threshold     model    DepMap      gap
largest gap 12.7%  (gate < 15%)   P2 PASS
P3 RANK -- among the 206 genes costing more than 1%, does the model rank them

P1 the gate was the problem             PASS
P2 the right amount of slack            PASS
P3 the slack is in the right places     FAIL
M3 WAS MEASURING NUMERICAL DUST. The model tolerates most single deletions at any
biologically meaningful threshold, and loop_medium's conclusion is corrected.
